feedback: Before this geometry races, the evidence is as follows. In iteration 0 (60 trials, zero completions), every run ended off track at about 0.062 m max error, with about one line-loss event per run. The loss happened at about the same offset where the robot left the track, which points to the five-sensor span (about ±0.058 m) as the limit. Iteration 0 also showed that the body width does not help, because the off-track limit stays at 0.06 m. I had to make the controller work with the existing sensor layout by keeping the weights proportional to lateral position, so the signal scale matches the offset. I kept the gains fixed to isolate the sensing change. Next race, if line_loss_events fall near 0 but max_error stays above 0.06 m, the controller gain or the reaction point is the limit: move the row closer to the axle or reduce the outer-sensor weights. If the robot stays on track but does not complete, the limit is speed: test a larger wheel radius and lower mass next. If line loss persists at the outer sensors, the 16 mm footprint may be overlapping too far, so try 12 mm at the same positions.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stay above about 0.5 per run while max_error is near 0.06 m: keep the seven-sensor span at ±0.06 m but reduce the footprint to 0.012 m, because iteration 0 used 12 mm footprints at 0.02 m pitch and still saw one loss per run.

If the robot stays on track (max_error under 0.06 m) but does not complete: try wheel_radius 0.035 m and mass 0.7 kg to reach speed, because iteration 0 never stalled and only failed by leaving the track.

If steering_oscillation rises on the slalom compared with iteration 0 (0.14 m): move the sensor row back to y = 0.04 m or reduce the outer sensors to x = ±0.05 m, because the earlier sensor row at y = 0.04 m gave a smoother but later reaction.
